newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian stocks end mixed in newfangled trade.
newsitem.headline: Colombian stocks end mixed in newfangled trade.

text.p: Colombian stocks ended mixed as the advent of electronic trading marked the end of an era at Bogota's 68-year-old stock exchange.

Medellin's IBOMED general price index closed up 0.24 percent at 13,625.29 on a paper-thin volume of 274.4 million pesos. Bogota's IBB index edged down 0.03 percent, closing at 869.50 on a volume of 1.5 billion pesos.
Brokers said the traditional month-end lull in trading was accentuated by Monday's launch of computerized trading system in Bogota, which virtually shut down the exchange's live trading floor.
The same system, known as Winset, will go into operation on Tuesday in Medellin and brokers said it will take some time to get used to.
Trading in the capital was heavily concentrated in Banco Anglo Colombiano, which fell 6.97 percent to close at 60 pesos per share on a cross trade involving 25 million shares.
The Bogota index was also weighed down by profit-taking in heavily traded Banco Ganadero, which saw its ordinary shares fall 0.35 percent to end at 284 pesos a share.
Cement maker Cementos Argos was also hit by profit-taking, dropping 0.36 percent to end at 5,410 pesos per share.
The rise in the Medellin index was fueled, at least in part, by a gain in Cementos Caribe of the powerful Sindicato Antioqueo industrial group.
The cement manufacturer closed up 2.47 percent at 4,100 pesos per share on a trading volume of 21.5 million pesos.
